why: Third most common class, 4 of the 16 videos, and chosen ahead of mass assignment (which shows up in 5) on cost: mass assignment only decides severity by reading the privileged column of the schema, and that requires a parser. This one is textual all the way through. The fail side compares with `===`, which proves there was no KDF -- bcrypt and argon2 return a salted hash and require `compare`. The pass side carries the false positive that matters: LEGITIMATE PRE-HASH. bcrypt truncates at 72 bytes without a word, and the recommended defense is to feed it a sha256 of the password. Whoever does that is RIGHT, and accusing them would punish the person who knows the problem -- which is why the fast-hash signal only holds where there is no slow primitive in the same file. The vocabulary is bilingual on both sides: both trees use `senha`, not `password`, because this module audits a Brazilian repository.
